summary: The Django admin login page (/admin/login) now sends users through the app's main sign-in (allauth) instead of its own password form, so staff who have two-factor authentication must enter their code to reach the admin; previously the admin login skipped 2FA.

statements.why: Nothing new is dangerous, but the card says plain reads logins and still says nothing about a login change (urls.py wraps admin.site.login with secure_admin_login) that closes a 2FA bypass on the admin page.
New test file; but the only code change (src/paperless/urls.py) isn't mentioned at all.

misses.what: Security fix: the admin site's login (/admin/) no longer accepts a plain username/password; it redirects to the normal sign-in page, so staff with two-factor authentication now must enter their code. Before this, the admin login let them skip 2FA.
Staff who used the admin's own login form now land on the main sign-in page instead.
